about_company.about_short: Makes aerospace tooling, precision parts and, since May 2026, metal bellows for global OEMs.
about_company.business_intro: Unimech machines the specialised tools that aircraft engine and airframe makers and maintenance shops use to build, assemble and service engines and aircraft, and makes precision parts and assemblies; since May 2026 it also makes metal bellows and exhaust systems through Hobel Bellows. It sells to a small set of global OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers, mostly in the United States: three customers were 72% of FY26 revenue, and 89% of FY26 revenue was exported.
about_company.about_long: Unimech Aerospace and Manufacturing makes engine, airframe and MRO tooling and ground support equipment that aircraft engine and airframe makers, their Tier-1 suppliers and maintenance shops use, working both to customer drawings (build to print) and to its own designs (build to spec) in high-mix, medium-to-low volumes. Tooling is the main business, at 76% of Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue. A smaller precision components and assemblies business serves aerospace, nuclear, semiconductor and energy customers and is still largely in qualification. Since 1 May 2026 the group also consolidates Hobel Bellows, a Visakhapatnam SEZ maker of metallic bellows and exhaust systems for engine makers, which was 21% of Q1 FY27 revenue on two months. Production runs from three Bengaluru facilities and Hobel's plant; a Saudi joint-venture unit with the Kanoo Group is being set up and is not yet operating. Exports were 89% of FY26 revenue, and Unimech holds about 30% of Dheya Engineering, whose micro gas turbine engines it has exclusive rights to manufacture.

company_timeline.title: Incorporated as Unimech Aerospace and Manufacturing
company_timeline.detail: Incorporated as a private limited company on 12 August 2016; it later converted to a public company.

company_timeline.title: Lists on NSE and BSE
company_timeline.detail: Trading began on 31 December 2024 after an IPO at ₹785 a share: a ₹250 crore fresh issue and an offer for sale of the same number of promoter shares.

company_timeline.title: Signs a 51:49 Saudi joint venture with the Kanoo Group
company_timeline.detail: Signed in January 2026 to set up a precision machining and remanufacturing unit in Dammam. No money had been invested by 31 March 2026, and in May 2026 management said the unit was still at a foundational stage.

company_timeline.title: Acquires Hobel Bellows
company_timeline.detail: Completed on 27 April 2026 for a 100% stake and a total investment of up to ₹450 crore. Management said the sellers were paid in cash with 10% held back for a year; the equity, debt and CCDs in the annual report fund Unimech's acquiring subsidiary. Consolidated from 1 May 2026.

company_timeline.title: Signs a long-term supply agreement with FACC
company_timeline.detail: Signed in Q1 FY27 with FACC Austria, an aerospace Tier-1, for aerostructure components: an initial USD 7.5 million over five years. Management calls it its first recurring aerospace component supply under a long-term programme.

business_facts.title: Three customers were 72% of FY26 revenue
business_facts.text: Three customers made up 72.37% of FY26 consolidated revenue from operations, down from 87.60% in FY25. The largest alone was 44.50% (FY25: 66.46%) and the next two 14.12% and 13.75%. These figures predate Hobel Bellows, where two OEM groups account for about 93% of revenue (management, April 2026).

business_facts.title: US was 76% of FY26 revenue; exports 89%
business_facts.text: In FY26, 89.4% of consolidated revenue from operations came from outside India: the United States 75.6%, Germany 9.7%, Canada 2.8% and the UK 0.8%. India rose to 10.6% from 5.2% in FY25, and the US share fell from 83.0%. The Q1 FY27 presentation puts exports at about 96% as on 30 June 2026, with Hobel included.

business_facts.title: Three Bengaluru plants plus Hobel's Visakhapatnam plant
business_facts.text: Unimech's Bengaluru footprint is a 150,000 sq ft aerospace tooling facility in the KIADB Aerospace SEZ at Devanahalli, a 93,000 sq ft precision components and assembly unit and a 30,000 sq ft fabrication facility. Hobel adds a 2,00,000 sq ft plant in the Visakhapatnam SEZ. The Q1 FY27 presentation counts five manufacturing facilities and a free-trade warehouse, about 5.6 lakh sq ft, including the Saudi joint-venture unit that is not yet operating. Management put utilisation at about 58% in Q1 FY27, with nearly 10% more committed to qualification work.

business_facts.title: Order book of ₹2,803 million at 30 June 2026
business_facts.text: The order book stood at ₹2,803 million on 30 June 2026: ₹1,802 million at Unimech, including an ₹873 million nuclear order, and ₹1,001 million at Hobel Bellows.

business_facts.title: 6,300+ qualified SKUs across 41 customers
business_facts.text: As on 30 June 2026 the company reported 6,300+ qualified SKUs (4,990 in tooling and 1,312 in precision components and assemblies), 41 customers in 8 countries and 1,232 employees including Hobel's. It executed 200+ first-article inspections in FY26 across aerospace and semiconductor customers.

business_facts.title: Hobel Bellows earned about ₹129 crore in FY26
business_facts.text: Hobel, established in 2007, makes metallic bellows, expansion joints, flexible metal hoses and exhaust assemblies for engine makers in power generation, locomotives and other industries. Management said it earned about ₹129 crore of revenue in FY26, before the acquisition, with an EBITDA margin above 50%, and has historically grown 10-15% a year. Exports are about 85% of its sales (Q1 FY27 presentation), against nearly 90% cited at the April 2026 acquisition call.

what_changed.headline: Dependence on the largest customer fell in FY26
what_changed.text: The largest customer's share of consolidated revenue from operations fell to 44.50% in FY26 from 66.46% in FY25, and the top three's to 72.37% from 87.60%. With total revenue roughly flat at ₹240.5 crore against ₹242.9 crore, sales to the largest customer fell by about a third while revenue from all other customers rose by about 64%. Revenue within India doubled to ₹25.4 crore. All of this is before Hobel Bellows was acquired.
